Definition: from G1223 and G4126; to sail through:--sail over.
BiblicalUsage: To sail over is to cross open water, and Luke uses it once on the voyage to Rome, when the ship sails over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia. It is a plain travel note from a man who was there.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Luke's sailing notes are the fingerprint of an eyewitness; he writes the sea's name because he crossed it, and the plainness of the detail is what makes the whole voyage ring true.
